title: Carry the pane tail and the unwind remedy on a failed herding spawn
action: In run.rs diagnose_giveup: when find_prompt_diagnosis returns None but pane_read succeeded, return format!("{generic}\npane tail:\n{tail}") using pane_tail; a failing pane_read still returns generic unchanged. Update the test diagnose_giveup_leaves_the_generic_message_byte_for_byte_on_no_match to assert the message starts with generic and contains 'pane tail:' and 'all green'; keep the failing-pane_read test as is. Then in the JSON output (around line 2461, RunOutcome::SpawnFailed arm only) add remedy: a string built by fn spawn_failed_remedy(cell_id: Option<&str>, agent: Option<&str>, pane_id: Option<&str>) -> String, e.g. 'inspect pane w5:pS (herdr pane read w5:pS); unwind: bee cells unclaim --id <cell>; bee reservations release --agent <agent> --cell <cell>' — omit the cells/reservations parts when cell_id is None and say 'no --cell-id was given, release any claim you took by hand'. Use opts.cell_id and the --agent name from opts (find its field). Add a unit test for spawn_failed_remedy. In swarming-reference.md herding section, add a short 'On spawn_failed' paragraph: the result JSON's remedy field names the unwind; claims and reservations stay the orchestrator's to release; the pane stays open as forensics.
acceptance: A no-match give-up error carries the pane tail; spawn_failed JSON carries remedy naming bee cells unclaim and bee reservations release; herding::run tests green; swarming-reference has the On spawn_failed paragraph.
